name: SEO Planner
description: Keyword distribution planner. Selects target keywords from keyword research and produces a flat keyword plan: target_keywords (primary/secondary/long_tail), meta title and description, optional FAQs, tone notes, and warnings. Section-level distribution is template-driven via format_spec.md. The manifest default is project-agnostic; pipeline-specific shape (e.g. company-profile categories/tags/credentials) is added via template prompt overrides. Uses configurable web search (Perplexity Sonar by default) to ground keywords in actual search patterns. Requires content-analyzer.
usage_notes: Requires content-analyzer output for keyword grounding. The manifest default produces a generic keyword plan; pipelines that need section-level keyword distribution (e.g. company profiles with categories/tags/credentials/faq sections) configure a template-level prompt override AND set requires_prompt_override = true to fail-loud if the override is missing. MODEL FLOOR (INFERRED BY ANALOGY — UNVERIFIED) — recommended minimum model: sonnet. This is NOT tested: Daniel's 2026-06 doc-non-compliance test covered content-analyzer, not seo-planner. seo-planner shares the same doc-following pattern (it reads format_spec.md / tone_guide.md and must honor a strict JSON output contract), so the risk that haiku reads its reference docs without complying is PLAUSIBLE here — but it has not been reproduced. Treat sonnet as the recommended floor pending a seo-planner-specific test; do NOT present this as tested. max_tokens RECONCILIATION: seo-planner is moving to sonnet alongside content-analyzer. Because sonnet is a Claude-5 model with adaptive thinking ON by default, the manifest default of 16384 is under-provisioned — it was sized for haiku (no thinking overhead), and sonnet's thinking consumes the budget invisibly, so 16384 can truncate and the skeleton fail-closed guard turns truncation into a run failure. A sonnet template MUST override max_tokens to 32768. The 16384 default (and the 'sized for haiku' option-description wording) are legacy haiku-era values, NOT the intended operating point. Perplexity Sonar runs configurable research queries per entity (1-5; 3 by default). Cost depends on configuration: at defaults (3 queries × sonar) ~$0.025/entity; at max (5 queries × sonar-reasoning-pro) ~$0.25/entity; disable via keyword_research: false for $0 research mode. Reference docs commonly used: format_spec.md and tone_guide.md when present — both are optional placeholders that degrade gracefully if not provided. CONTENT GATE (v2.3.2): after the plan parses, seo-planner asserts it yields at least one usable keyword/head term (the exact condition meta-compliance-checker reads); a valid-but-empty plan fails LOUD with meta.status:'error' (entity turns red) instead of shipping a hollow plan as success — see README. KEYWORD-RESEARCH CONTEXT (v2.3.3): the Perplexity research seed ({entity_context}) is derived GENERICALLY from the analyzer output (not a fixed field list), so research targets the real entity subject instead of collapsing to the bare entity name (run 85bc05e1: 'X is in the X space'). On a content-gate (hollow) failure the raw model output is captured onto the error item + meta (raw_response) so the next hollow plan is diagnosable from output_data, not inferred.

options.name: ai_model
options.label: AI Model
options.description: Which model to use for SEO planning.

options.name: keyword_research
options.label: Keyword Research
options.description: Run web search research before SEO planning. Researches actual keywords from the web instead of relying on LLM general knowledge.

options.name: search_provider
options.label: Search Provider
options.description: Which search API to use for keyword research. Perplexity Sonar is the default. More providers (Gemini, Ahrefs, Semrush) can be added later.

options.name: perplexity_model
options.label: Perplexity Model
options.description: Which Perplexity Sonar model to use for keyword research. sonar = cheapest, fastest. sonar-pro = better quality, more expensive. sonar-reasoning = chain-of-thought capable for complex queries. sonar-reasoning-pro = top-tier reasoning. Cost ranges from ~$0.005/query (sonar) to ~$0.05/query (sonar-reasoning-pro).

options.name: research_queries
options.label: Research Queries
options.description: Search queries to run before SEO planning. Multi-line queries are supported when delimited by `Query N —` markers; any text before the first marker is treated as shared preamble prepended to every query. Templates without markers fall back to one-query-per-line. Use {entity_name} for the entity name and {entity_context} for a short context summary extracted from the analysis.
options.default:
Context: {entity_name} is in the {entity_context} space. Match the keyword research to the AUDIENCE this entity actually serves (infer audience from the context — e.g. B2B operators, end consumers, job seekers, procurement teams — and exclude queries from audiences that don't apply).

Query 1 — Core keywords:
What keywords does {entity_name}'s actual target audience search for? Return three buckets:
- 1 primary phrase (the entity's core offering in the audience's language)
- 2-4 secondary phrases (main product/service categories)
- 3-5 long-tail phrases (specific differentiators, often the entity name + a category)
Return source URLs you found these in.

Query 2 — Competitor positioning:
Find the top 3-5 pages currently ranking for the {entity_context} space. For each page, list 2-3 keyword phrases it targets and one sentence on its angle (what problem the page solves, who for). Include URLs. Do NOT estimate search volume or competition level — you do not have keyword-tool data and any numbers would be invented.

Query 3 — Real audience questions:
List exactly 12 real search queries that {entity_name}'s audience types when researching this entity or similar {entity_context}. Mix:
- 3 'what is / who is' definitional queries
- 3 'vs / compared to / alternative' comparison queries
- 3 'how does X handle Y' or 'X integration / X pricing / X compliance' operational queries
- 3 problem-framed queries (the underlying problem the audience has)
These will be used VERBATIM as FAQ questions in the content, so use natural phrasing as people actually type, not keyword-stuffed phrasings. Include source URLs proving each is a real search pattern.

options.name: reference_docs
options.label: Reference Documents
options.description: Reference docs for SEO planning. Common docs: format_spec.md (defines section structure if the template uses one), tone_guide.md (voice rules). Optional fallback: keyword-summary.md is read ONLY when keyword_research is disabled or returns no results.

options.name: temperature
options.label: Temperature
options.description: LLM temperature for SEO planning. Lower = more consistent keyword mapping. Default 0.3 for structured planning.

options.name: max_tokens
options.label: Max output tokens
options.description: Maximum tokens in the LLM response. Sized for haiku (no thinking overhead); complete section-level plans run 4k-7k+ tokens (largest observed ~23k chars). If you switch this module to a Claude-5 model (sonnet/opus), adaptive thinking consumes this budget invisibly — raise it or truncation fails the run.

options.name: faq_count
options.label: FAQ Count (agnostic default)
options.description: Number of FAQ questions the agnostic manifest default prompt asks for. Default 0 (no FAQs). This option only takes effect on the agnostic path — when a template override is in use, the override prompt's own FAQ instructions are authoritative and faq_count is ignored unless the override prompt explicitly uses the {faq_count} placeholder.

options.name: requires_prompt_override
options.label: Requires Prompt Override (per-template)
options.description: If true and the prompt at runtime equals the manifest default (no template override configured), seo-planner refuses the run early with a clear error. Default false (the manifest default is a valid generic run path). Templates that depend on section-structured output (categories/tags/credentials/faq sections, etc.) should set this true and configure a prompt override so a missing override fails loud instead of silently producing an unexpectedly generic plan.

options.name: keyword_data_providers
options.label: Keyword data providers
options.description: Quantitative keyword-data providers (v2.3.0) — real search volume, difficulty, and own-site rank/impressions from SEO/search APIs, ALONGSIDE the qualitative (Perplexity) research. Array of provider config objects; each names a `kind` that selects a generic handler. Built-in kinds: `gsc` (Google Search Console — free, own verified properties only), `dataforseo` (paid volume/difficulty), `autocomplete` (free seed expansion). Empty (the default) = layer is fully inert, zero cost, output unchanged. See README for the config schema. Feed the numbers into the LLM by adding {keyword_metrics} to your prompt override; the fetched metrics always land in seo_plan_json.keyword_metrics regardless.

options.name: max_seed_keywords
options.label: Max seed keywords
options.description: Cap on seed keywords sent to expansion/metrics providers per entity. Cost guard. Only applies when keyword_data_providers is non-empty.

options.name: max_metric_lookups_per_entity
options.label: Max metric lookups per entity
options.description: Hard cap on keyword→metrics lookups per entity (seeds + expansion). Cost guard. Only applies when keyword_data_providers is non-empty.

options.name: per_run_budget_usd
options.label: Per-entity keyword-data budget (USD)
options.description: Sums each provider's est_cost_per_lookup; refuses further PAID lookups once the cap would be exceeded, warns loudly, and continues with free providers (GSC, autocomplete). Cost guard. Only applies when keyword_data_providers is non-empty.

options.name: metrics_required
options.label: Require keyword metrics
options.description: If true and all metrics providers fail, are inert, or return empty, add a loud warning to the plan's warnings[] (never silent) — surfaces upstream provider/credential problems instead of quietly planning without numbers. Default false. Only applies when keyword_data_providers is non-empty.

options.name: prompt
options.label: Planning prompt
options.description: The prompt sent to the AI. Use {entity_content} for analysis JSON, {keyword_research} for keyword research results, {faq_count} for the configurable FAQ count (agnostic path only), and {doc:filename} for reference doc content. The manifest default is fully project-agnostic. Pipeline-specific shapes (e.g. company-profile section breakdowns) belong in template prompt overrides.
options.default:
You are an SEO strategist. Produce a keyword distribution plan for the content writer to follow. You do NOT decide the article structure (the format spec, if provided, defines it). You do NOT write the content. You produce a keyword plan only.

### INPUTS

**Analysis from content-analyzer:**
{entity_content}

**Keyword research data (from the configured search provider, e.g. Perplexity web search):**
{keyword_research}

If the keyword research block above says 'No keyword research data available' or appears empty/low-quality, the keyword research step did not produce usable output. In that case: (1) add a warning to the JSON output's `warnings` array — the text 'Keyword research returned no data — keywords were inferred from content-analyzer categories/tags only. Review this output before publishing.' Do NOT emit this warning as a markdown heading or any text before the JSON object. (2) Tag every keyword in `keyword_sources` as 'analysis' rather than 'Q<n>'. (3) Proceed using the analysis as the sole source. Do NOT silently produce a plan as if the research succeeded.

**Format rules (uploaded reference doc — defines the section structure if provided):**
{doc:format_spec.md}

**Tone rules (uploaded reference doc — voice rules if provided):**
{doc:tone_guide.md}

### CRITICAL RULE — KEYWORD SOURCING

Every keyword you place into the plan MUST come from the keyword research block above. Do NOT invent keywords from your training data. Do NOT add keywords because 'they sound right.' If the keyword research didn't surface a phrase, it is not in scope for this plan.

The keyword research is grounded in actual web search patterns. Your training data is not. Trust the research, not your priors.

Exception: entity-specific long-tail phrases — constructed from the entity name + a category or differentiator found in the research — are permitted even if the exact phrase isn't in the research output.

### INSTRUCTIONS

Create an SEO plan as a JSON object. Follow these rules exactly:

**1. TARGET KEYWORDS**

Select keywords from the keyword research data. Cross-reference against the analysis to filter for relevance.
- `primary`: 1 phrase that best describes this entity's core offering, in the language the audience actually uses
- `secondary`: 2-4 phrases covering main product/service areas
- `long_tail`: 3-5 specific phrases

For every keyword selected, record its provenance in the `keyword_sources` field — name the query number (Q1, Q2, ... QN) it came from, or 'analysis' if derived from content-analyzer's categories/tags per the CRITICAL RULE exception.

**2. KEYWORD DISTRIBUTION**

If a format spec was provided in {doc:format_spec.md} above, map keywords to the sections defined there using whatever section names that format spec uses. If no format spec was provided, return `keyword_distribution: {}` (an empty object) — the content writer will work from `target_keywords` directly. Do NOT invent sections that are not in the format spec.

**3. META TAGS**

- `title`: ≤60 characters. Lead with the entity name and primary value proposition.
- `description`: 150-160 characters. One compelling sentence summarizing the entity and its value prop, including the primary keyword naturally.
- Include character counts for both.

**4. FAQS**

Produce exactly {faq_count} FAQ question(s).

If {faq_count} is 0, return an empty array: `faqs: []`. Skip the rest of this section.

If {faq_count} is greater than 0:
- Select questions from the keyword research data (real audience questions surfaced by the research)
- Use them VERBATIM, or with minimal substitution to make them entity-specific
- Do NOT invent FAQ questions from your own knowledge — if the research didn't surface a question, it does NOT go in the FAQ
- If fewer than {faq_count} research questions are answerable from the analysis content, output only the answerable subset and add a warning
- Each question's `answer_brief` is a short direction note for the writer (NOT the actual answer)
- Each question's `target_keyword` is a long-tail keyword from the research that the answer should weave in

**5. TONE NOTES**

One short paragraph describing the tone for this entity's content.

**6. WARNINGS**

Flag any issues in the `warnings` array:
- Meta length problems (title >60 chars, description outside 150-160 range)
- Thin source material (analysis doesn't support keyword targets)
- Keyword gaps (research didn't surface keywords for an area in the analysis)
- FAQ shortage (fewer answerable research questions than {faq_count} requested)
- Research absence (the keyword research block was empty or low-quality)

### OUTPUT FORMAT

Return ONLY a valid JSON object matching this schema:

```json
{
  "target_keywords": {
    "primary": "string",
    "secondary": ["string"],
    "long_tail": ["string"]
  },
  "keyword_sources": {
    "primary": "Q<n> | analysis",
    "secondary": ["Q<n> | analysis"],
    "long_tail": ["Q<n> | analysis"]
  },
  "keyword_distribution": {},
  "meta": {
    "title": "string",
    "title_chars": 0,
    "description": "string",
    "description_chars": 0
  },
  "faqs": [
    {
      "question": "string",
      "answer_brief": "string — direction for writer, not the actual answer",
      "target_keyword": "long-tail keyword this FAQ targets"
    }
  ],
  "tone_notes": "string",
  "warnings": ["string"]
}
```

The first character of your response MUST be `{` and the last character MUST be `}`. No markdown headings before, after, or inside the JSON. No code fences. No explanation. No preamble. Return ONLY the JSON object.
